params.body:
## Why

The list that is being brought into `/newsletter-admin` has a remarks column, and the remarks say things the organisation wants to keep seeing next to a person: how they know them, which school, who to greet. The list had no field for them, so an import would have left them behind in the old sheet. And because an import never touches a person it already knows, a second import could not have added them afterwards.

## What changes

- **Import**: a column titled Remarks, Notes, Opmerkingen, Remarques (and a few close variants) is taken along. Without a title for it, no remark is read, so a sheet without column names cannot turn a stray cell into a remark.
- **Add one person**: a Remarks field.
- **The list**: the remark shows under the email address, the search finds it, and a "Remark" link per row changes or removes it.
- **Downloads**: the backup has a Remarks column. The download to send from does not, so a remark cannot end up in a mail merge.
- **Privacy text** (NL, FR, EN): says a short remark may be kept with a subscription. Date of the text updated.

A remark is one line of at most 500 characters. It is stored on the subscriber document, which is readable only with the token like the rest of the list.

## Checked

- `npm test`: 80 pass, 3 of them new (remarks column under its English, Dutch and French titles; no remark without a title; the 500 character limit).
- `npm run build` passes.
- The page was looked at in a browser with four made-up people, at desktop and phone width.

## Not checked

The write to the real dataset. It uses the same calls as the rest of the list.

## After merging

Nothing to run. The import of the existing list is best done after this is live, so that its remarks come along.
params.title: A remark can be kept with each person on the newsletter list
